newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power falls amid unit restarts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power falls amid unit restarts.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. ended weaker Monday against Friday's levels as a couple of Tennessee Vally Authority's (TVA) nuclear generating units returns from unplanned outages.
"Everything is dumping," said one Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC) trader.
TVA's 1,065 MW Browns Ferry 2 nuclear power unit in Decatur, Ala., and 1,148 MW Sequoyah nuclear unit 2 in Soddy Daisy, Tenn., were restarted this past weekend.
"When TVA sells power cheap...people start panicking," the SERC trader said.

TVA was heard offering next-day, non-firm peak electricity for Tuesday at $22.00 a megawatt hour (MWh). The largest U.S. electric utility had been absent from selling power in the daily market due to the outages of those two nuclear units.
In the northwestern part of TVA's (TVA) territory, firm, peak electricity for Tuesday delivery was assessed at $18.00-$20.00, lower than Friday's $20.00-21.00 area.
Firm, next-day power for delivery into northwestern TVA during light load hours on Tuesday was notationally pegged at $12.00-$14.00.
Despite the startup of the TVA units, there was still considerable amount of generation, which was unexpectedly idled in the past couple of months.
Florida Power Corp's 860 megawatt (MW) Crystal River 3 nuclear power plant in Red Level, Fla., remained shut amid review of its 19 year old design and equipment operations.
In SERC, Duke Power Co's two McGuire nuclear units in Cornelius, N.C., are shut down, depleting a combined 2,258 megawatts (MW) from the market.

Another 2,538 MW have been missing from the market due to the outages at Duke Power's three Oconee nuclear units in Seneca, N.C. The units are not expected to return to service in mid-November as was scheduled, but the exact restart dates were not available.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity for Tuesday delivery was quoted at $21.00-$22.50 a megawatt hour (MWh), down from Friday's $25.00-26.00 for weekend delivery.
Firm, off-peak power for Tuesday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally valued at $14.00-$15.00, down from Friday's $15.00-$18.00.
According to latest forecasts, weather in the Southeast including Florida was predicted to turn milder through mid-week, but to cool from seasonal norms by week's end.
